nodes.title: Browser window shows a border on higher dpi on multi monitor setup (black when dark theme, white when light theme)
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 42.3.3 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 42.3.2 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Window should look normal ### Actual Behavior Window has a black border On the left how it should look like (electron 42.3.2) On the right how it looks now (electron 42.3.3) ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/t57ser/ebb9bd6838088521d0ebd6ec8644f84f ### Additional Information single display: happens only when changing the scaling while the app runs, otherwise the border is not visible even if the screen has a scaling multi display: if the primary display is a lower scale than the secondary it will happen either when moving the window there or when creating the window on the secondary screen i.e. 125% 100% (primary) - creating on 125% => has border - creating on 100% and moving to 125% => has border if the primary screen has a scaling then it will only happen if the secondary screen has a higher scaling i.e. 150% 125% (primary) 100% - moving from 125% to 150% => border - moving from 125% to 100% => no border

nodes.title: [Bug]: Notification 'click' never emitted on macOS for banners presented while the app is frontmost
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- I have read the contributing guide and searched existing issues: no macOS report of this exists (the post-migration notification regressions on file are Windows-only, e.g. #51147, #51650).

### Electron Version

42.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.7.1 (any 41.x — the pre-UNUserNotificationCenter backend)

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a notification banner emits `click` on the `Notification` instance regardless of whether the app is frontmost. This was the behavior of the `NSUserNotification` backend, whose delegate fired `didActivateNotification` on `ContentsClicked` independent of focus (and presented foreground notifications via `shouldPresentNotification: YES`).

### Actual Behavior

Since the migration to `UNUserNotificationCenter` (#47817, shipped in 42), a banner presented while the app is frontmost (via `willPresentNotification` → `Banner | List | Sound` in `shell/browser/notifications/mac/notification_center_delegate.mm`) just dismisses when clicked: macOS never invokes `didReceiveNotificationResponse` for it, so `NotificationClicked()` never runs and no `click` is emitted.

Clicking the same notification while the app is backgrounded or minimized works (the normal delivered-notification activation path).

Ruled out: this is not the garbage-collection issue (#16922) — references are retained — and not the unsigned-build case (the app is code-signed and notifications display and emit `show` normally).

### Testcase Gist URL

Not reproducible in Fiddle: since 42, macOS notification events require a code-signed app. Steps with a signed build:

1. On 42.1.0, while the app window is focused, `new Notification({title: 'x'}).show()` (delayed a few seconds behind a timer) with a `click` listener attached and the reference retained.
2. Click the banner → no `click` event.
3. Same steps with the app unfocused or minimized → `click` fires.
4. Same steps on 41.x → `click` fires in all cases.

### Additional Information

We hit this in production (Basecamp Desktop): users reported notification clicks "doing nothing", exactly and only when the window was active. Downgrading to 41.7.1 restored the old behavior, which is our current mitigation.

Reading the 42-x-y delegate code, the dispatch itself looks correct (`UNNotificationDefaultActionIdentifier` → `NotificationClicked()`, identifier lookup intact) — the response callback simply never arrives from macOS for foreground-presented banners. If that's an OS-level contract of `UNUserNotificationCenter`, it would be worth documenting as a breaking change of the migration; if there's a way to opt foreground banners back into response delivery, even better.

🤖 Drafted with AI assistance; the analysis above was verified against the `42-x-y` sources.

nodes.title: Frameless non-resizable `BrowserWindow` reports incorrect bounds since v41.5.0.
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 23H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.4.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`getBounds()` returns `{ width: 500, height: 75 }` matching the constructor values.


### Actual Behavior

`getBounds()` returns `{ width: 484, height: 67 }` — 16px narrower, ~8px shorter.


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/3ed4b0642f381e3ee11628a3672ae990

### Additional Information

### Key Observations

- Only affects `resizable: false` windows — `resizable: true` works correctly
- Only affects `frame: false` windows — framed windows unaffected
- Reproducible at scale factor 1.0, so NOT a HiDPI/scaling issue
- Offset matches typical Windows shadow/border insets (8px per side)
- Introduced between 41.4.0 → 41.5.0

**Electron Version:** 41.5.0+ (regression from 41.4.0)
**OS:** Windows (confirmed with scale factor 1.0 and 2.0)
**Platform:** Windows 10/11

---

### Summary

Frameless non-resizable `BrowserWindow` reports incorrect bounds since v41.5.0.
The actual window is smaller than the requested size by a fixed margin:
- Width: −16px (8px each side)
- Height: −8~9px (bottom only)

This suggests window frame/border insets are being incorrectly subtracted
from the client area even when `frame: false` is set.

---

### Regression Range

| Version  | Scale 1.0 | Scale 2.0 |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| 41.4.0   | ✅ Correct | ⚠️ Off by 1px height only |
| 41.5.0   | ❌ −16w/−8h | ❌ −16w/−7h |

---

The Sample result:

```
41.4.0✅
Scale factor: 2
--- resizable: false ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   500 x 76
--- resizable: true ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   500 x 75

Scale factor: 1
--- resizable: false ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   500 x 75
--- resizable: true ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   500 x 75

41.5.0 ❌
Scale factor: 2
--- resizable: false ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   484 x 68
--- resizable: true ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   500 x 75

Scale factor: 1
--- resizable: false ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   484 x 67
--- resizable: true ---
Expected: 500 x 75
Actual:   500 x 75

```

nodes.title: [Bug]: globalShortcut on Wayland never calls the host `Registry.Register` portal handshake, so `register()` fails on xdg-desktop-portal ≥ 1.20 (GNOME 50)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). - [x] I have searched for existing issues. Closest are #49873, #48391, #45607, #49806 — all closed/fixed and present in the versions tested below; none cover the `Registry.Register` requirement. ### Electron Version(s) Reproduced on **40.6.1, 41.5.0, 41.7.1, and 42.3.3** (latest). All identical. ### What operating system(s) are you using? Linux (Fedora 44, Wayland) ### Operating System Version Fedora 44 Workstation, GNOME Shell 50.2, **xdg-desktop-portal 1.21.2**, xdg-desktop-portal-gnome 50.0 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown on this portal version. The related accelerator/app-id fixes (#49988 → backported to `41-x-y` via #50051) are present in all versions tested here, but do not resolve this. ### Expected Behavior With `--enable-features=GlobalShortcutsPortal` and `--ozone-platform=wayland`, `globalShortcut.register('CommandOrControl+Alt+Space', cb)` should register a global shortcut via the XDG GlobalShortcuts portal and fire `cb` regardless of which window is focused. ### Actual Behavior `globalShortcut.register(...)` returns **`false`** and `isRegistered(...)` is **`false`**. A full session-bus trace shows the renderer **never contacts `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts`** (no `CreateSession`, no `BindShortcuts`) and **never calls `org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry.Register`**. The shortcut effectively degrades to focus-bound. Toggling the feature on/off makes **no difference** on Wayland; the same MRE returns `true` on `--ozone-platform=x11`: | ozone backend | `GlobalShortcutsPortal` flag | `register()` | portal `CreateSession` calls | |---|---|---|---| | wayland | enabled | `false` | 0 | | wayland | default (no flag) | `false` | 0 | | wayland | disabled | `false` | 0 | | x11 (XWayland) | enabled | `true` | 0 (X11 grab) | ### Root cause (diagnosed) xdg-desktop-portal **1.20+** requires a non-sandboxed ("host") app to declare its identity by calling **`org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry.Register(app_id, options)`** before app-id-gated portals will serve it. Chromium's `GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux` still relies on the legacy systemd-scope app-id derivation: in a bus trace it creates `app-electron-.scope` but never calls `Registry.Register`. On xdg-desktop-portal 1.21 the legacy path no longer yields an app id for host apps, so: ``` $ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop \ --object-path /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop \ --method org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts.CreateSession "{...}" Error: org.freedesktop.portal.Error.NotAllowed: An app id is required ``` **Proof the portal itself is fully functional** — a minimal Python client that performs the missing `Registry.Register` call (with a reverse-DNS app id backed by a `.desktop` file) drives the whole flow successfully and receives `Activated` from an unfocused window: ``` Registry.Register('com.example.GsPortalProof') OK CreateSession OK -> .../session/1_7016/session1 BindShortcuts OK -> id='open-quick-entry' trigger='Press space' *** ACTIVATED *** id='open-quick-entry' (press #1) *** ACTIVATED *** id='open-quick-entry' (press #2) ``` Secondary note: GNOME's backend additionally rejects app ids that are not reverse-DNS and backed by an installed `.desktop` file (`gnome-control-center-global-shortcuts-provider: Discarded shortcut bind request from application with an invalid app_id >gsportalproof<`). Electron's default app id (the executable name, e.g. `electron`) would likely also fail this even once `Registry.Register` is wired up — so both the `Registry.Register` handshake **and** a valid `.desktop`-backed reverse-DNS app id are needed. ### Testcase **Electron MRE** (`register()` returns `false`): ```js const { app, globalShortcut, BrowserWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { new BrowserWindow({ width: 320, height: 120 }); const acc = 'CommandOrControl+Alt+Space'; const ok = globalShortcut.register(acc, () => console.log('FIRED')); console.log('register returned', ok, 'isRegistered', globalShortcut.isRegistered(acc)); }); // run: electron --ozone-platform=wayland --enable-features=GlobalShortcutsPortal . ```
Python client proving the portal works once Registry.Register is called Run wrapped in a matching systemd app scope + `.desktop` file: ``` # ~/.local/share/applications/com.example.GsPortalProof.desktop with # Name=GS Portal Proof, Exec=python3 .../gs_portal_proof.py systemd-run --user --scope -u app-com.example.GsPortalProof.scope \ python3 gs_portal_proof.py ``` ```python import dbus from dbus.mainloop.glib import DBusGMainLoop from gi.repository import GLib PORTAL, OBJ = "org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop", "/org/freedesktop/portal/desktop" GS = "org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts" REG = "org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry" APP_ID = "com.example.GsPortalProof" DBusGMainLoop(set_as_default=True) bus = dbus.SessionBus() portal = bus.get_object(PORTAL, OBJ) sender = bus.get_unique_name()[1:].replace(".", "_") # THE MISSING STEP: declare the host app id on this connection. dbus.Interface(portal, REG).Register(APP_ID, {}) def req(tok): return f"{OBJ}/request/{sender}/{tok}" def on_created(code, res): sh = res["session_handle"] def on_bound(c, r): print("BindShortcuts code", int(c)) bus.add_signal_receiver(lambda c, r: on_bound(c, r), signal_name="Response", dbus_interface="org.freedesktop.portal.Request", path=req("bind1")) shortcuts = dbus.Array([dbus.Struct(("open-quick-entry", dbus.Dictionary( {"description": dbus.String("demo"), "preferred_trigger": dbus.String("CTRL+ALT+space")}, signature="sv")), signature="sa{sv}")], signature="(sa{sv})") dbus.Interface(portal, GS).BindShortcuts(sh, shortcuts, "", {"handle_token": "bind1"}) bus.add_signal_receiver(lambda c, r: on_created(int(c), r), signal_name="Response", dbus_interface="org.freedesktop.portal.Request", path=req("create1")) bus.add_signal_receiver(lambda *a: print("*** ACTIVATED ***", a[1]), signal_name="Activated", dbus_interface=GS) dbus.Interface(portal, GS).CreateSession( {"handle_token": "create1", "session_handle_token": "sess1"}) GLib.MainLoop().run() ```
### Additional Information - The portal advertises `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts` version 1 and `org.freedesktop.host.portal.Registry` with `Register(sa{sv})`. - Likely fundamentally a Chromium bug in `ui/base/accelerators/global_accelerator_listener/global_accelerator_listener_linux.cc` (the listener should perform the host `Registry.Register` handshake on xdg-desktop-portal ≥ 1.20), surfacing through Electron's `globalShortcut`. Happy to file/cross-reference upstream in the Chromium tracker if preferred.

nodes.title: [Bug]: Buffer.byteLength/Buffer.from compute wrong UTF-8 size for large strings with non-ASCII chars; fs.writeFileSync aborts
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.2, 42.3.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon (M1 Max)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

v42.3.0

Standalone Node 24.10.0 (V8 13.6) behaves correctly.

### Expected Behavior

`Buffer.byteLength(s, 'utf8')` returns the correct UTF-8 byte count, `Buffer.from(s, 'utf8')` round-trips, and `fs.writeFileSync(path, s, 'utf-8')` writes the file.

### Actual Behavior

For large strings containing a non-ASCII character, the UTF-8 size is computed wrong, `Buffer.from` silently produces a truncated/corrupted buffer, and `fs.writeFileSync` hard-aborts the whole process with an uncatchable C++ CHECK:

```
Assertion failed: (length + 1) <= (capacity())
void node::MaybeStackBuffer<char>::SetLengthAndZeroTerminate(size_t) [T = char, kStackStorageSize = 1024]
  at ../../third_party/electron_node/src/util.h:454
```

Repro (run with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, also reproduces in the main process):

```js
const s = 'a'.repeat(200000) + 'ç' + 'a'.repeat(199999)

console.log(s.length)                      // 400000
console.log(Buffer.byteLength(s, 'utf8'))  // 399999 — wrong, should be 400001

const b = Buffer.from(s, 'utf8')           // 399999 bytes, silently corrupted
console.log(b.toString('utf8') === s)      // false (round-trips to length 399998)

require('fs').writeFileSync('/tmp/x', s, 'utf-8')  // aborts the process (SIGTRAP)
```

On Electron 42.3.2 (Node 24.15.0, V8 14.8.178.28-electron.0) all three are broken as above. On standalone Node 24.10.0 (V8 13.6.233.10-node.28) all three behave correctly.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/nikwen/a26e64f8b377086aa52740e8f9b94e5c

### Additional Information

I hit this in production: my app persists a JSON stats file that had grown to ~600 KB and contained a couple of `ç`/`ã` characters. Every save aborted the main process a few seconds after launch (uncatchable CHECK), which is how I found it.

A few data points from bisecting:

- Pure-ASCII strings of any size are fine; at least one non-ASCII char is needed.
- A non-ASCII char within the last few code units of the string does not trigger it.
- The length dependence is non-monotonic, which suggests sensitivity to the string's internal representation rather than plain size — with a single `ç` in the middle: len 131072 OK, 200000 crash, 262144 OK, 262146 crash, 300000 OK, 400000 crash.
- It also reproduces with a flat string read via `fs.readFileSync` (not only concatenated/cons strings).

The silent `Buffer.from` corruption seems worse than the abort — anything encoding large user strings to UTF-8 can write truncated data with no error at all.

nodes.title: Removing a shadow-hosted iframe with nodeIntegrationInSubFrames can throw "illegal access" when setImmediate is pending
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched for an existing issue that matches this behavior.
- [x] I have included a minimal reproduction repository.

### Electron Version

42.0.0, 39.1.0

### What operating system are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Expected Behavior

Removing a DOM node that hosts an iframe in its shadow root should not throw synchronously. In the reproduction, `document.body.removeChild(host)` should succeed regardless of whether a `setImmediate` callback is pending in the parent renderer.

### Actual Behavior

When `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` is enabled and the iframe has loaded with Node/Electron runtime available, removing the shadow host while a `setImmediate` callback is pending throws:

```text
removeChild threw: illegal access
```

The same DOM removal succeeds when `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` is disabled.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/6700965200910b47de74fbd6710996ce

### Additional Information

The minimal trigger appears to be:

1. Create a `BrowserWindow` with `nodeIntegration: true`, `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: true`, `contextIsolation: false`, and `sandbox: false`.
2. In the main frame, create a host element and attach an open shadow root.
3. Append an iframe inside that shadow root and load a local HTML file that uses `require('electron')`.
4. Wait for the iframe `load` event.
5. Queue a parent-frame `setImmediate(() => {})` callback.
6. Immediately call `document.body.removeChild(host)`.

Observed comparison from the repro:

- With `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: true`: iframe reports `require=function`, and `removeChild` throws `illegal access`.
- With `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: false`: iframe reports `require=undefined`, and `removeChild` succeeds.

A pending `setTimeout(..., 0)` or Promise microtask did not reproduce the exception in the same test shape; the failure seems specific to pending `setImmediate` while detaching a node-enabled subframe hosted inside shadow DOM.

nodes.title: Distro Packaging and `process.argv` (and others)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Packaging Electron applications in distros is a bit weird. We want the packages to be as close to the experience of it being from the upstream application repo as possible, while also getting regular security updates.

The way that distos (Arch and Nixpkgs at least) generally do this is the following:
1. Package supported Electron versions
2. Package the application `resources` directory (primarily the `.asar`, but also sometimes other files)
3. Add a wrapper than does something like `/bin/electron41 /share/CoolElectronApplication/resources/app.asar`

This works decently well. It decouples the Electron from the application so it can be updated separately. But there are a few snags.

* Doing this naively, Electron considers itself "unpackaged" and so `app.isPackaged` is false

This primarily results in logging being output by applications. Disto wrapping solves this with the magic `ELECTRON_FORCE_IS_PACKAGED`. Set this to true, and now `app.isPackaged` returns true. 

Great! Now dev logging isn't output. But at what cost? This does break applications, subtlety. This breaks `process.argv`. The only thing the above environment variable changes is the output of `app.isPackaged` outputting true. It does not change the order of `process.argv` to be the "packaged" format. This is NOT changed if `app.isPackaged` returns true, but when `app.getPath('exe')` returns something that isn't `electron`. 

A common pattern in applications is doing something like:
```js
  if (app.isPackaged) {
    process.argv.unshift(null)
  }
```
or something similar (`process.argv.slice(app.isPackaged ? 1 : 2)` is also common). When `ELECTRON_FORCE_IS_PACKAGED` is set, this is incorrect! The format is not the "packaged" argv, so CLI arguments become incorrect. 

We noticed this in Nixpkgs, and attempted to work around it with a shim that attempts to setup all the paths correctly.
https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/487711#issuecomment-4594210912

This almost works! `process.argv` is correct, `app.getPath('exe')` is correct, `app.isPackaged` is true, and `resourcesPath` is correct. Testing this shim, what fails is `app.relaunch`. 
https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat.Electron/blob/3c89e81c7bc41ba742178d3f84070817e6e05f25/src/app/main/app.ts#L85

Unfortunate. I tried some other solution, like making a symlink of `Electron` to see if that changed the way it considers itself "packaged," but it does not. So we are pack to the original status quo. This *mostly* works because most Electron apps don't take CLI args, so breakage is not common. 

### Proposed Solution

Some way to tell Electron "hey this is packaged!" without needing to jump thru hoops with an imperfect shim that lies to Electron about what's running, and duplicates Electron logic. I do not know exactly what. I know users want:

1. The application name to appear in `top` (this currently does not happen)
2. Dev logging not to output
3. Don't bloat package size (aka don't copy Electron into every every Electron application)

And then use distro maintainers would like:

1. Something low maintenance (not duplicating Electron processing logic)
2. Possibly at build time? Would be nice not to need runtime flags. 

### Alternatives Considered

Status-quo. Currently things work *fine*. Not perfect, but fine. 

### Additional Information

https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/electron42/-/blob/main/electron-launcher.sh

Nixpkg's wrapper (they are currently ad-hoc, trying to fix that) look something like:
```bash
export ELECTRON_FORCE_IS_PACKAGED=1
exec /nix/store/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-electron/bin/electron /nix/store/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa1-application/share/resources/application/resources/app.asar "$@"
```

nodes.title: Dirent.parentPath is missing from fs.glob/globSync withFileTypes under asar
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Ventura 13.5 (arm64), Windows 11 25H2 (x64)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`fs.glob` or `fs.globSync` with `options.withFileTypes` expect to return `fs.Dirent[]` under asar packaged or not. And the `fs.Dirent` should include a `parentPath` property.

```ts
// dist/index.js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

const direntList = fs.globSync('*.js', { cwd: import.meta.dirname, withFileTypes: true })
/*
[
  Dirent {
    name: 'index.js',
    parentPath: '/path/to/project/dist',
    Symbol(type): 1
  }
]
*/
```

### Actual Behavior

`Dirent.parentPath` property is existing under dev runtime `npx electron .` or build `asar: false`, but it's missing under asar packaged.

```ts
// under asar packaged app
// dist/index.js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { dialog } from 'electron'

const direntList = fs.globSync('*.js', { cwd: import.meta.dirname, withFileTypes: true })

// Use showErrorBox to print value after build app.
dialog.showErrorBox('', JSON.stringify(direntList, null, 2))
/*
[
  {
    "name": "index.js"
    // parentPath is missing
  }
]
*/
```

Dirent.parentPath is a relatively new property. It's marked stable in node.js `v24.0.0` and `v22.17.0`. Maybe hasn't been implemented yet in electron asar mode.
https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#direntparentpath

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The following steps can be used to reproduce the result. Using node.js `v24.15.0` same with electron's node.js version.

1. Create a new npm project directory and enter it
```bash
$ mkdir electron-test
$ cd electron-test
$ npm init --y
```

2. Install dependencies
```bash
$ npm install -D electron@42.2.0 electron-builder@26.8.1
```

3. Edit electron-builder config in package.json
```jsonc
// package.json
{
  // ...
  // add the following
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "type": "module",
  "build": {
    "appId": "some.app.id",
    "compression": "store",
    "asar": true,
    "directories": {
      "output": "release"
    }
  }
}
```

4. Add `dist/index.js`
```js
// dist/index.js
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { app, dialog } from 'electron'

const direntList = fs.globSync('*.js', { cwd: import.meta.dirname, withFileTypes: true })

// print value
console.log(direntList)
dialog.showErrorBox('', JSON.stringify(direntList, null, 2))

app.exit()
```

5. Run `npx electron .` the Dirent.parentPath exists
6. Run `npx electron-builder` to build app with asar
7. Click to launch the packaged app, we can see the `Dirent.parentPath` is missing in the dialog

nodes.title: NAN 2.27.0 incompatible with V8 13.x (Electron 42 / Node 24): v8::External API breaking changes
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 23H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.7.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

NAN should handle the v8::External API change in V8 13.x, as it has
handled previous V8 API changes, so addons using NAN compile against
Electron 42 / Node 24 without modification.

### Actual Behavior

## Description
Building any NAN-based native addon against Electron 42 (V8 13.x) headers 
fails due to breaking changes in `v8::External` API:

- `v8::External::Value()` now requires a `v8::Isolate*` parameter
- `v8::External::New()` signature changed

The errors originate inside NAN's own files:
- `nan_callbacks_12_inl.h`
- `nan_implementation_12_inl.h`

## Error Output
```
nan_callbacks_12_inl.h(213,46): error C2660:
'v8::External::Value': function does not take 0 arguments
nan_implementation_12_inl.h(79,24): error C2660:
'v8::External::New': function does not take 2 arguments
```


## Minimal Reproduction

**binding.gyp**
```json
{
  "targets": [{
    "target_name": "hello",
    "sources": [ "hello.cc" ],
    "include_dirs": [ "<!(node -e \"require('nan')\")" ]
  }]
}
```

**hello.cc**
```cpp
#include <nan.h>

NAN_METHOD(Hello) {
    info.GetReturnValue().Set(
        Nan::New("hello world").ToLocalChecked()
    );
}

NAN_MODULE_INIT(Init) {
    NAN_EXPORT(target, Hello);
}

NODE_MODULE(hello, Init)
```

**package.json**
```json
{
  "name": "nan-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "nan": "2.27.0" },
  "scripts": { "build": "node-gyp rebuild" }
}
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
```bash
npm install
# Download Electron 42 headers
npx node-gyp rebuild --target=42.3.0 --dist-url=https://electronjs.org/headers
```


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_
